guitar.modelsText: Gibson Les Paul Standard ("Greeny", ex-Peter Green)
models: Gibson Les Paul Standard ("Greeny", ex-Peter Green)
guitar.notes: Confirmed and refined — Gary Moore's 1959 Les Paul "Greeny" (previously owned by Peter Green) is one of the most famous guitars in blues-rock history.

tone.target: singing Gary Moore sustain with creamy Marshall lead
tone.profile: singing Gary Moore sustain with creamy Marshall lead
tone.summary: A classic British lead tone chain using OD boost for initial drive, followed by a powerful UK 45 amp model, paired with a vintage 4x12 cabinet to achieve singing sustain and articulate bends.
corrections: aim for vocal lead, not rhythm

rig.name: Gary Moore - Parisienne Walkways - Valeton GP-180

blocks.purpose: Clean up ambient noise and hum.
Provide gentle boost and sustain enhancement for singing bends.
Add mid-forward grit and controlled saturation for lead tone.
blocks.gap: The RAT is often aggressive; careful settings are needed to keep it creamy rather than crunchy. Using a lower drive setting helps achieve the desired sustain without excessive dirt.

blocks.purpose: Emulate the classic Marshall British lead tone and provide core saturation.
Provide the classic British cabinet sound and frequency response.
Slightly scoop the low end and boost mids to enhance vocal clarity and lead presence.
Simulate the wide vibrato characteristic of Gary Moore's playing.
blocks.gap: A dedicated Vibrato module would be ideal, but Tremolo is used to achieve a controlled, noticeable pitch wobble effect.

blocks.purpose: Add subtle echo and space without washing out the lead lines.
Add subtle natural ambience to round out the sound.

improvements.summary: Enhance cabinet realism with an IR that better captures the creamy, articulate Marshall lead tone.

proposals.reason: The current IR is generic; a specific Marshall cab will improve the creamy, articulate lead tone.
proposals.expectedGain: Increased realism and depth in the high-mids.
